replies.raw:
Here's a wild fact to start: when you type the word "unbelievable" into ChatGPT, the model doesn't see that word at all.

It sees three chunks: **"un"**, **"believ"**, **"able"** — each converted to a number.

---

That's **tokenization** — the very first thing that happens when you hit send.

Every piece of text gets sliced into tokens, which are common chunks of letters (not always whole words). Each token maps to a unique number in a vocabulary of roughly 100,000 entries.

---

So "I went to the bank" might become five tokens: `[40, 1816, 284, 262, 3331]`.

The model never reads letters. From the first millisecond, it's working entirely in numbers.

---

Here's where it gets interesting: the word "bank" is ambiguous — river bank or money bank?

A tokenizer alone can't tell. That ambiguity gets passed forward into the model, and something else has to sort it out. (We'll get there.)

---
